incidents-bot: ALERT: High tail latency detected for `inference-api` continuous-batching path in us-west2. p99 = 6.2s, p95 = 1.4s, error rate +0.6%. Paging: @alex (oncall). :rotating_light:

alex (oncall): ack. I'm oncall and looking. First glance: p99 spike started ~03:15 UTC. Any recent deploys?

samir: I see a spike in `pack_time_ms` and a jump in cont-batch queue depth. Linking dashboards: https://rdw/graphs/contbatch/usw2/p99-pack-time

jess: fyi we ran a small scheduler tweak at 03:12 UTC to change `fairness_window` and bump `max_batch_size` from 64 -> 96 for the hetero-scheduler canary. Commit: 7a4d2b3. Could be related.

alex (oncall): confirmed. 03:12 deploy from `eng-runtime` -> canary target: contbatch-scheduler. Running quick diffs on telemetry. Raw snapshot: ```
p95 latency: 1.4s
p99 latency: 6.2s
pack_time_ms median: 12ms
pack_time_ms p99: 2100ms
queue_depth p99: 48
streams_stalled: 0.8%
```

maria (sre): who has permission to roll back scheduler canary? If this is the cause we should revert to prev config. Alternatively, we can temporarily set `max_batch_size=48` and `preemptive_shed=true` to reduce pack amplification.

jess: I can push a config tweak to the canary in 1-2 mins. Rolling back the binary will take longer and might increase churn. Proposed quick mitigation: `echo '{"max_batch_size":48,"preemptive_shed":true}' | rctl apply contbatch/canary-config --env=us-west2`

alex (oncall): doing the config patch now. Running command: ```bash
rctl apply contbatch/canary-config --set max_batch_size=48 --set preemptive_shed=true --region usw2
```

ops-bot: deploybot: config apply succeeded for contbatch/canary-config @ 1712349945

alex (oncall): monitoring... initial effect: p99 dropped to ~1.1s within 40s. p95 steady ~0.9s. Streaming stalls count improved but still seeing some individual stalls.

kev (cust-ops): any customer visible errors? We had a report from tenant AcmeCorp at 03:18 with higher response times, no 5xx but timeouts for streaming long responses. Do we need to notify customers?

alex (oncall): good catch. I see increased streaming client timeouts for requests with seq_len > 1400 tokens. Those requests hit pack_time p99 and got delayed. Logged sample: ```
[2026-03-15T03:17:22Z] request_id=abc123 tenant=acme seq_len=1420 pack_ms=1873 serve_ms=36 total_ms=1910
```

jess: that aligns: increasing `max_batch_size` caused packs to accumulate more heterogeneous sequences, amplifying padding/serialize time. The scheduler fairness tweak prioritized throughput but increased tail for hetero workloads.

samir: from metrics, the majority of affected requests are mixed-seqlen streaming (chat + long context). We should: 1) keep canary config change, 2) enable `kv_prefix_cache` warmup for canary nodes, 3) open RCA ticket for scheduler heuristics.

alex (oncall): applied cache warmup to canary: `kv-cache warmup --prefix chat-* --region usw2` — confirmed warming. Next 5m window looks stable: p99 0.95s, p95 0.85s, streams_stalled 0.12%.

maria (sre): great mitigation. Let's not revert scheduler commit yet; keep the conservative config in canary and push a safety flag into prod only after further regression tests. Also drag in the model-routing folks to verify no quality regressions due to batching change.

jess: creating a short-lived experiment to split hetero traffic to a smaller batch-size pool. Config snippet I pushed to experimentation: ```json
{
  "routing": {"seqlen_based_pooling": true, "split_threshold": 1024},
  "pool_config": {"small_batch":{"max_batch_size":32}, "standard":{"max_batch_size":48}}
}
```

kev (cust-ops): do we need to send a proactive note to tenants that may have seen degraded latency? AcmeCorp is asking for incident details.

alex (oncall): suggest holding a short notification with: root cause suspected scheduler config change + mitigation (reduced max_batch_size + kv warmup) + current impact (transient p99 spike, resolved for most traffic). I'll draft a customer note after this thread. @kev please review.

samir: logging: I captured a stacktrace sample from a stalled stream — shows contention in `pack_queue::wait_for_pack` with long waits during the hetero packing path. We'll add more sampling at pack boundaries and surface `pack_wait_ms` in the dashboards.

maria (sre): also add a regression test in CI for mixed-seqlen workloads with fairness window variations. Ticketing: create an incident ticket and assign to `eng-runtime` + `eng-sre` for 72h follow-up.

incidents-bot: Incident 2026-1712349999 created: "contbatch-heterolen-tail-spike-usw2" severity: SEV3. Status: mitigated -> monitoring. Link: https://rdw/incidents/2026-1712349999

alex (oncall): summary for handoff: 
- Trigger: deploy + scheduler tweak at 03:12 UTC bumped `max_batch_size` up for hetero canary
- Impact: p99 tail spike up to 6.2s, streaming client timeouts for long seq_len (>1400) observed for ~4min
- Mitigation: lowered `max_batch_size` to 48 on canary, enabled `preemptive_shed`, warmed kv-cache -> p99 back to ~0.9s
- Next steps: roy (eng-runtime) to run regression + tuning of fairness heuristics, add pack_wait_ms metric, consider seqlen-based routing pools

alex (oncall): handing off to morning oncall @maria (sre). I'm filing the RCA stub and attaching metrics. Leaving canary config in conservative state until after regression sign-off.

maria (sre): ack. I'll take ownership overnight, will schedule postmortem if we identify process gaps. +1 on customer notification draft.

kev (cust-ops): thanks all — please send me the customer-facing blurb once ready. I'll coordinate comms with AcmeCorp. :thumbsup:

jess: quick note — we'll block the `max_batch_size` bump for hetero-scheduler unless a performance test shows no tail amplification. Adding to PR checklist.

alex (oncall): closing thread from ops side. If anything regresses ping this channel. Great work triaging quickly. :heart:
